title: DID verify blocks tokio executor (CPU crypto)
description: verify_did_sig in run_post_pipeline is called directly on the tokio async executor without spawn_blocking. The function includes ed25519_dalek::VerifyingKey::verify_strict, a CPU-bound crypto operation (~50-100 µs on modern hardware), plus base58 decode and base64 decode. Tokio's async executor threads are designed for I/O-bound work; CPU work on an executor thread blocks that thread from servicing other futures for the duration. Under burst POST load (e.g. a feed spike or a reconnect storm), multiple concurrent sessions each calling verify_did_sig simultaneously will saturate executor threads with CPU work rather than I/O. Fix: wrap the verify_did_sig call in tokio::task::spawn_blocking so it runs on the blocking thread pool, which is sized separately and does not starve the I/O executor.
